The `[edat]` clause is the fixed 2018-11-17 cutoff for this run, applied to PubMed entry date. It isn't a publication-date limit.

`work/` also holds `audit.md`, `validation-manifest.json` and `narrative.md`.

**Recall:** the strategy retrieves 10 of the 11 benchmark records (90.9%). This is relative recall, not sensitivity.
- You had no known articles. I built the benchmark from the PubMed reference lists of two prior reviews (30075313 and 29475431) and screened them by title only.
- The benchmark is thin: 8 of the 11 records come from one review. The lower bound on recall is 63.6%.
- The one miss is 21731066, "Neural mechanisms of the cognitive model of depression". Its abstract names neither relapse nor recurrence, so I accepted it as out of reach.

**Assumptions and risks:**
- **Scope:** I treated the scope as kept without your confirmation. It has two searched concepts: depression, and relapse or recurrence.
- **Theory not searched:** "Psychological theory" is not in the search. I tested it as an optional block, and adding it would cut the result to 11,392 records. I left it out because you asked for high sensitivity, and the measured evidence is too weak to say it would lose nothing. The 95% bound allows a loss of up to about 26%. You'd screen all 18,503 records with theory as a screening criterion. If that is too many, you can reverse this.
- **OpenAlex:** it was unavailable because its budget was used up, so I found known records through PubMed only.
- **Critic:** one critic round ran (an internal check, not PRESS peer review). Its one syntax finding was fixed, and the only remaining concern is the missed record above.
